caption: Try to avoid closing roads.
content: We will refer to a state where a continuous road can no longer be extended in any direction as the road being @b{closed}.
For example, both of the following roads are closed.
On the other hand, the following road is not closed, because you can still place a road tile at the cell @m{pending}.

To complete an Area, @g{rule/complete_block/road}{all roads must form a single connected network}. Once a road is closed, it can no longer be extended to connect to other roads. Be careful not to close a road while there are still other roads that need to be connected.

content.caption: Example
content: Assuming your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_road.2t.dl} @t{forest_road.2t.ul} @t{forest_road.2t.ur}, let's solve this Area.
First, if we focus on the cell @m{pending}, there are two tiles that can be placed here: @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dl}.
If you place @t{forest_road.2t.dl}, the cell below can only take @t{forest_road.2t.ul}, which causes the road to become closed as follows.

Even if you place more road tiles, the roads will not form a single connected network, and you won't be able to complete the Area. So, we can see that placing @t{forest_road.2t.dl} on the cell @m{pending} was a mistake.
Therefore, the tile on the cell @m{pending} must be @t{forest_road.2s.lr}, which also determines the tile for the cell below.
By repeating this deduction, the Area will be completed as follows.
